item.text: The files are aligned as a 59,453-gene expression matrix, matching gene metadata, and 723 annotated samples. I found explicit `celltype` labels and a `gene_biotype` field, so I’m using those rather than inferring cell types from sample names. Next I’m validating sample coverage, gene identifiers, and missing/negative values before calculating the correlations.

item.text: The direct analysis is decisive: using all annotated samples and all 19,942 protein-coding genes, the correlations are CD4 0.06170, CD8 0.05513, CD14 0.03169, and CD19 0.04711. CD14 has the smallest absolute value. The same ordering holds for reference/non-reference sample subsets and for a log-transformed mean-expression sensitivity check; I’m doing one independent implementation check before writing the required one-line output.

/bin/bash -lc "if command -v Rscript >/dev/null 2>&1; then Rscript - <<'RS'
meta <- read.csv('inputs/GeneMetaInfo_Zenodo.csv', row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
ann <- read.csv('inputs/Sample_annotated_Zenodo.csv', check.names=FALSE)
x <- read.csv('inputs/BatchCorrectedReadCounts_Zenodo.csv', row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(x), rownames(meta)), identical(colnames(x), ann"'$sample))
pc <- meta$gene_biotype == '"'protein_coding'
cts <- c('CD4','CD8','CD14','CD19')
r <- sapply(cts, function(ct) cor(meta"'$Length[pc], rowMeans(x[pc, ann$celltype == ct, drop=FALSE]), method='"'pearson'))
print(r, digits=12)
cat('weakest:', names(which.min(abs(r))), '\\n')
RS
else echo 'Rscript unavailable; primary standard-library calculation already completed'; fi"
